reasoning: The reviewer asked only for a wording change on FIG. 1 but the preflight required the sheet be split for exceeding eight numerals. Those two instructions conflict on the FIG. 1 numeral list, and the gate is the harder constraint, so I removed one numeral rather than leaving the list intact. I chose 52 (mating channel) because FIG. 3 already shows that recess and the rib entering it at enlarged scale, so nothing is lost; the recess stays on FIG. 1 as an unnumbered feature, which keeps the exploded view intelligible without a second referent for a numeral.

The preflight named only FIG. 1, but FIG. 2 listed ten numerals and the old FIG. 4 listed twelve. Fixing only what was named would have moved the same failure to the next sheet on the next run, so I brought the whole set within the limit in this turn.

FIG. 2 lost numerals 12 and 50 rather than being split, because it is the orientation view whose job is the closed circulation loop: the loop bullets (26, 28, 30, 40, 44) are what that sheet exists for, while the shell floor is shown in detail on the wick sheet and the outlet opening on the outlet sheet. Per the numeral-move rule, the canonical part names 'shell floor' and 'peripheral outlet opening' were also removed from FIG. 2 and replaced with generic unnumbered bodies.

The old FIG. 4 was carrying two unrelated subjects at once: lid-to-upper-edge sealing with foot-on-ledge retention, and the duct outlet with condensate discharge. Splitting on that natural seam gives seven numerals per sheet and matches the specification's own division between the registration and retention paragraph and the condensate handling paragraph, so each figure now supports one written passage.

I renumbered downstream (wick becomes FIG. 6, indicator becomes FIG. 7) rather than appending the new sheet at the end, so the figures still run outside-in and top-down in the order the description walks through them.

The FIG. 1 emptiness fix follows the reviewer's substance but omits numerals 18 and 70 from the sentence, because listing them would have put them on the sheet's numeral list and pushed FIG. 1 back over the limit for parts that are deliberately not drawn there. The unnumbered phrasing mirrors the indicator sheet, which the reviewer identified as the correct convention.

FIG. 2 and FIG. 1 exceeded the 2800-character brief limit after these edits, so I condensed both. The cuts were redundant phrasing and detail that is carried at enlarged scale on a focused sheet; the disclosed relationships (tray suspended above the floor, passages open at the top of the tray walls, outlet gap overlapping the side supply passage, tongue entering the recess, gasket band between lid underside and wall top) all remain stated.

No prior art is listed in prior_art/INDEX.md, and this turn changed no claim, so the claim set and its distinguishing feature (the depending indexing rib shifting the module into the position where the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, completing a closed fan-free path) stand as drafted.

structured_output.summary: Cleared both filing-gate failures. FIG. 1 was over the eight-numeral sheet limit and asserted an empty shell interior that contradicted the interior structure shown in the sectional views. Numeral 52 (mating channel) was moved off FIG. 1 to FIG. 3, where the rib-and-channel engagement is already shown enlarged, and the FIG. 1 shell bullet now states expressly that the ledges and the shallow condensate channel are not shown in this view, matching the omission convention already used on the indicator sheet. Checking the rest of the set, FIG. 2 listed ten numerals and the old FIG. 4 listed twelve, so both were brought within the limit as well: FIG. 2 now shows the shell floor and the peripheral outlet opening as unnumbered context (they carry their numerals on the focused sheets), and the old FIG. 4 was split into a sealing-and-retention sheet (FIG. 4) and an outlet-and-condensate-discharge sheet (FIG. 5), with the wick sheet renumbered FIG. 6 and the exposure-indicator sheet renumbered FIG. 7. The FIG. 2 callout paragraph, the Brief Description of the Drawings, and every figure reference in the Detailed Description were resynchronized. FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 were condensed to stay under the 2800-character brief limit. No claim, summary, background, abstract, or numeral-table text was changed, and no structure, relationship, or dimension was added.
reasoning: The reviewer asked only for a wording change on FIG. 1 but the preflight required the sheet be split for exceeding eight numerals. Those two instructions conflict on the FIG. 1 numeral list, and the gate is the harder constraint, so I removed one numeral rather than leaving the list intact. I chose 52 (mating channel) because FIG. 3 already shows that recess and the rib entering it at enlarged scale, so nothing is lost; the recess stays on FIG. 1 as an unnumbered feature, which keeps the exploded view intelligible without a second referent for a numeral.

The preflight named only FIG. 1, but FIG. 2 listed ten numerals and the old FIG. 4 listed twelve. Fixing only what was named would have moved the same failure to the next sheet on the next run, so I brought the whole set within the limit in this turn.

FIG. 2 lost numerals 12 and 50 rather than being split, because it is the orientation view whose job is the closed circulation loop: the loop bullets (26, 28, 30, 40, 44) are what that sheet exists for, while the shell floor is shown in detail on the wick sheet and the outlet opening on the outlet sheet. Per the numeral-move rule, the canonical part names 'shell floor' and 'peripheral outlet opening' were also removed from FIG. 2 and replaced with generic unnumbered bodies.

The old FIG. 4 was carrying two unrelated subjects at once: lid-to-upper-edge sealing with foot-on-ledge retention, and the duct outlet with condensate discharge. Splitting on that natural seam gives seven numerals per sheet and matches the specification's own division between the registration and retention paragraph and the condensate handling paragraph, so each figure now supports one written passage.

I renumbered downstream (wick becomes FIG. 6, indicator becomes FIG. 7) rather than appending the new sheet at the end, so the figures still run outside-in and top-down in the order the description walks through them.

The FIG. 1 emptiness fix follows the reviewer's substance but omits numerals 18 and 70 from the sentence, because listing them would have put them on the sheet's numeral list and pushed FIG. 1 back over the limit for parts that are deliberately not drawn there. The unnumbered phrasing mirrors the indicator sheet, which the reviewer identified as the correct convention.

FIG. 2 and FIG. 1 exceeded the 2800-character brief limit after these edits, so I condensed both. The cuts were redundant phrasing and detail that is carried at enlarged scale on a focused sheet; the disclosed relationships (tray suspended above the floor, passages open at the top of the tray walls, outlet gap overlapping the side supply passage, tongue entering the recess, gasket band between lid underside and wall top) all remain stated.

No prior art is listed in prior_art/INDEX.md, and this turn changed no claim, so the claim set and its distinguishing feature (the depending indexing rib shifting the module into the position where the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, completing a closed fan-free path) stand as drafted.

figures/FIG-4.md: rewritten as the sealing and retention detail at the upper right, showing shell side wall 14, upper edge 16, ledge 18, rigid spacer frame 42, resilient foot 54, insulated lid 60, and compressible lid gasket 64, with the guide duct shown as an unnumbered open passage (7 numerals).

figures/FIG-5.md: rewritten as the outlet and condensate discharge detail at the lower end of the right-hand duct, showing shell side wall 14, tray side wall 24, side supply passage 30, rigid spacer frame 42, downward guide duct 48, peripheral outlet opening 50, and condensate discharge opening 56 (7 numerals).

figures/FIG-7.md: added, carrying the mechanical exposure indicator view formerly numbered FIG. 6, keyed to the left-hand broken circle in FIG. 2 (6 numerals).

draft/08-detailed-description.md: figure references updated to the new set (FIG. 1 through FIG. 7; overview to FIG. 1, FIG. 2, and FIG. 6; tray paragraph to FIG. 2, FIG. 5, and FIG. 6; module paragraph to FIG. 1, FIG. 3, FIG. 4, and FIG. 5; retention paragraph to FIG. 4 and FIG. 5; condensate paragraph to FIG. 5 and FIG. 6; indicator paragraph to FIG. 7).
structured_output.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references for this application, so there is no citation to add or adjust and nothing in the Background was altered. The independent claims were not touched this turn; claim 1 continues to rest on the lid-driven registration, that is, the depending indexing rib entering the mating channel as the lid closes and thereby shifting the removable thermal module into the position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, which is what closes the fan-free circulation loop through the central inlet opening, the opposed cassette faces, the downward guide ducts, the side supply passages, the tray perforations, and the lower return passage. The dependent ladder keeps the seal-after-registration ordering, the resilient feet on the ledges, the condensate discharge into the wick channel, and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator as separately arguable fallbacks. The figure split reinforces that record by giving the registration and retention geometry and the outlet overlap their own enlarged sheets rather than one crowded view.
structured_output.answer: Both filing blockers are resolved and the whole drawing set now passes the sheet limits. FIG. 1 no longer states that the shell interior is empty; it states instead that the ledges and the shallow condensate channel are not shown in that view, which is the same convention the indicator sheet uses, so the shell is depicted consistently across the set without adding any line work. To bring FIG. 1 within the eight-numeral limit, the mating channel numeral moved to FIG. 3, where the rib entering the channel is already shown enlarged; FIG. 1 keeps the recess as an unnumbered feature. Two further sheets were over the same limit, so they were fixed in the same pass: FIG. 2 now shows the shell floor and the peripheral outlet opening as unnumbered context, and the crowded right-hand detail was split into FIG. 4 (gasket compressed against the upper edge, resilient foot bearing on the ledge) and FIG. 5 (peripheral outlet opening overlapping the side supply passage, condensate discharge opening at the duct's lower end). The wick view is now FIG. 6 and the mechanical exposure indicator view is now FIG. 7. The FIG. 2 callout paragraph, the Brief Description of the Drawings, and every figure reference in the Detailed Description were updated to match. FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 were also condensed to stay under the brief length limit, cutting only redundant phrasing and detail that appears at enlarged scale on a focused sheet. Every numeral still has exactly one part, appears on at least one sheet, and each sheet's numeral list matches the parts its brief describes. Claims, summary, background, abstract, and the numeral table are unchanged.
